Definition: feminine of φοῖβος (bright; probably akin to the base of G5457); Phœbe, a Christian woman:--Phebe.
BiblicalUsage: Phoebe is a servant of the church at Cenchrea, and Paul commends her to the Romans. He asks them to receive her in the Lord, as becomes saints, and to assist her in whatever business she has need of, for she has been a succourer of many, and of Paul himself also.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Phoebe's commendation is the church's letter of reference: a woman who helped many, trusted to carry the greatest letter ever written.
